import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Mean value problem

*Reference:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_value_problem)
- [The fundamental theorem of algebra and complexity theory](https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1981-04-01/S0273-0979-1981-14858-8/)
by Steve Smale

Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there is a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ K* |p'(z)|$ for $K=1$.


The conjecture has been proven for:
* `K = 4`
  [The fundamental theorem of algebra and complexity theory](https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1981-04-01/S0273-0979-1981-14858-8/)
  by *Steve Smale*
* `K = (d-1)/d` if $p$ has real roots or all the roots of $p$ have the same norm.
  [Critical points and values of complex polynomials](https://doi.org/10.1016/0885-064X(89)90019-8)
  by *David Tischler*
-/

namespace MeanValueProblem

/--
Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there is a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ |p'(z)|$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.degree) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ):
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
The following weaker version of the mean value problem has been proven.
Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ 4|p'(z)|$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_leq_4 (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.degree) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ):
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ 4 *‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
The following tighter bound depending on the degree $d$ of the polynomial $p$,
in the case of $p$ only having real roots has been shown by Tischler.
$|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| \le (d-1)/d \cdot |p'(z)|$
-/

@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_of_real_roots (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.natDegree)
    (h : ∀ x : ℂ, p.IsRoot x → x.im = 0) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ (p.natDegree - 1)/ p.natDegree * ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
The following tighter bound depending on the degree $d$ of the polynomial $p$,
in the case of $p$ all roots having the same norm has been shown by Tischler.
$|p(z) - p(c)|/|z-c| \le (d-1)/d \cdot |p'(z)|$.
-/

@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_of_roots_same_norm (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.natDegree)
    (h : ∀ x y : ℂ, p.IsRoot x ∧ p.IsRoot y → ‖x‖=‖y‖) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ (p.natDegree - 1)/ p.natDegree * ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

end MeanValueProblem

findings.description: The real-root restriction is applied to p, but the conclusion is asserted at every complex z. Tischler's special case concerns the normalized polynomial f with f(0)=0, evaluated at 0. For a general evaluation point, the relevant polynomial is q(X)=p(X+z)-p(z); its real-root condition is not the hypothesis currently written. For example, p=X^3-X has real roots, but at z=2i its normalization is X^3+6iX^2-13X, with roots 0, 2-3i and -2-3i. No nonzero complex scaling makes the latter two roots simultaneously real. These calculations were verified in Lean. Thus the usual normalization does not justify the file's unrestricted z.
findings.source_evidence: J. Illán González's review of Tischler, Critical points and values of complex polynomials (1989), Zbl 0728.12004, first reduces the problem to the normalized objective S_i=f(θ_i)/(θ_i f′(0)), and then describes the (d-1)/d result for polynomials with all roots real. Read via https://api.zbmath.org/v1/document/_structured_search?Title=Critical%20points%20and%20values%20of%20complex%20polynomials . The Wikipedia partial-results sentence suppresses this normalization.
findings.suggested_fix: State the normalized special case: add p.eval 0 = 0, evaluate the conclusion at z=0, and retain the real-root hypothesis. The source's noncritical hypothesis p.derivative.eval 0 ≠ 0 may also be included; omitting only that hypothesis is harmless by the critical-point extension. Alternatively, to retain arbitrary z, move z before h and replace h by `∀ x : ℂ, p.eval x = p.eval z → x.im = z.im`, the exact real-root condition on p(X+z)-p(z). Update the accompanying prose accordingly.

findings.description: This uses equal norms of all roots of p and an arbitrary evaluation point z. Tischler's result instead concerns the nonzero roots of the normalized polynomial f with f(0)=0, at the evaluation point 0. Both the exclusion of the distinguished zero and the normalization matter. The standard example X^3-X satisfies the intended nonzero-root condition, but fails the file's hypothesis because its roots include 0 and 1; this distinction was verified in Lean. For arbitrary z, the condition must concern the other points in the fibre p⁻¹(p(z)), measured by their distances from z—not the norms of the zeros of p.
findings.source_evidence: The review of Tischler (1989), Zbl 0728.12004, explicitly says “all the nonzero roots of f have the same norm” in the normalized formulation: https://api.zbmath.org/v1/document/_structured_search?Title=Critical%20points%20and%20values%20of%20complex%20polynomials . Independently, Crane's thesis, Topics in Conformal Geometry and Dynamics, p. 130 defines the normalized family by p(0)=0 and p′(0)=1; Theorem 5.6, p. 137, attributes to Tischler the result where “the roots of q(z)=p(z)/z all lie on the unit circle.” See https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~maetc/thesis.pdf .
findings.suggested_fix: Use z=0, add p.eval 0 = 0, and require equal norms only for roots x,y with x≠0 and y≠0. Alternatively, retain arbitrary z and replace h by `∀ x y : ℂ, p.eval x = p.eval z → p.eval y = p.eval z → x ≠ z → y ≠ z → ‖x - z‖ = ‖y - z‖`, moving z before this hypothesis. This is exactly the transported nonzero-root condition; its equivalence to the normalized condition was proved in Lean. Correct the module summary and theorem docstring as well.

status_issues.source_status: The cited Wikipedia page now records the K=1 conjecture as disproved on 3 September 2026, crediting GPT-6 Astra in collaboration with Tom Adamczewski. It describes a normalized polynomial with p(0)=0, p′(0)=1, and |p(c)/c|>1 at every critical point.
status_issues.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_value_problem , revision 1373726000, section “Disproof (2026)”: “On 3 September 2026, Smale's mean value conjecture for K=1 was formally disproved…”
status_issues.suggested_change: Update the category to research solved and record the negative resolution, for example using `answer(False) ↔` the universally quantified original conjecture, or a negated conjecture statement. This is a status/answer update, not a misformalization of the original problem.

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement allows critical evaluation points z and does not explicitly require c≠z. It also uses a quotient of norms instead of the norm of a complex quotient.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: If p′(z)=0, choose c=z: Lean's total division makes the left side 0, and the right side is 0. If p′(z)≠0, every critical point c automatically differs from z. Finally, ‖a/b‖=‖a‖/‖b‖ for complex numbers. Thus the universal Lean statement is equivalent to the usual formulation restricted to noncritical z, with c≠z and the norm of the quotient. The additional unused real parameter is logically redundant because ℝ is inhabited.

reformulations.difference: As with the main conjecture, the statement extends Smale's usual noncritical-point formulation to all z and uses a quotient of norms.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same equivalence was proved in Lean for an arbitrary real coefficient κ, hence in particular for κ=4: critical z are handled by c=z, noncritical z ensure c≠z, and norm_div identifies the two expressions. This extension does not weaken the substantive assertion.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked. Lean confirmed that (p.natDegree - 1)/p.natDegree is real arithmetic, that the two degree conventions exclude zero and constant polynomials identically, and that critical points exist under the degree hypotheses. Quadratic boundary cases and satisfiability of both root predicates were tested. Successful independent experiments are in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, boundaries.lean, normalization.lean, and transformed_hypotheses.lean; none uses the conjectures as proof premises. The original Smale (1981) and Tischler (1989) full texts were blocked by their publishers. Smale's statement was checked through Crane's explicit restatements; Tischler's special cases were checked through the review of that paper and Crane's theorem. The newly reported disproof was not independently proof-checked, and no linked repository or repository review was consulted. No repository files were edited; the target's contents match the committed file.

demonstrated.claim: The cubic p=X³−X satisfies the file's degree and real-root hypotheses, but the transported real-root condition at z=2i fails because p(2−i)=p(2i) while their imaginary parts differ.
The cubic p=X³−X has p(0)=0, p′(0)≠0 and all nonzero roots of norm 1, but the file's equal-norm hypothesis fails on its roots 0 and 1.

submission.summary: Created /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean with two short, independent hypothesis-discrepancy examples. These do not prove or refute either full mean-value inequality, and they do not use the admitted problem lemmas. The required Lean compilation completed without errors or warnings.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.MeanValueProblem

/-! Concrete hypothesis discrepancies, not disproofs of the mean-value inequalities. -/

-- MeanValueProblem.mean_value_problem_of_real_roots: p = X^3 - X satisfies h,
-- but normalization at z = 2i has the non-real root 2 - 3i.
-- The transported real-root condition is p(x) = p(z) → Im x = Im z.
example :
    let p : Polynomial ℂ := Polynomial.X * (Polynomial.X - 1) * (Polynomial.X + 1)
    2 ≤ p.natDegree ∧
      (∀ x : ℂ, p.IsRoot x → x.im = 0) ∧
      ¬ (∀ x : ℂ, p.eval x = p.eval (2 * Complex.I) → x.im = (2 * Complex.I).im) := by
  intro p
  have hp : p.natDegree = 3 := by dsimp only [p]; compute_degree!
  refine ⟨by omega, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x hx
    simp [p, Polynomial.IsRoot, mul_eq_zero, sub_eq_zero, add_eq_zero_iff_eq_neg] at hx
    rcases hx with (hx | hx) | hx <;> simp [hx]
  · intro h
    have hw := h (2 - Complex.I) (by
      norm_num [p, Complex.ext_iff, Complex.mul_re, Complex.mul_im])
    norm_num at hw

-- MeanValueProblem.mean_value_problem_of_roots_same_norm: p = X^3 - X has
-- nonzero roots of norm 1, but the file's h fails on its roots 0 and 1.
example :
    let p : Polynomial ℂ := Polynomial.X * (Polynomial.X - 1) * (Polynomial.X + 1)
    2 ≤ p.natDegree ∧ p.eval 0 = 0 ∧ p.derivative.eval 0 ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ x : ℂ, p.IsRoot x → x ≠ 0 → ‖x‖ = 1) ∧
      ¬ (∀ x y : ℂ, p.IsRoot x ∧ p.IsRoot y → ‖x‖ = ‖y‖) := by
  intro p
  have hp : p.natDegree = 3 := by dsimp only [p]; compute_degree!
  refine ⟨by omega, by norm_num [p], by norm_num [p], ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x hx hx0
    simp [p, Polynomial.IsRoot, mul_eq_zero, hx0, sub_eq_zero, add_eq_zero_iff_eq_neg] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> norm_num
  · intro h
    have h01 := h 0 1 (by norm_num [p, Polynomial.IsRoot])
    norm_num at h01

submission.summary: Normalized both Tischler special cases at 0, adding p(0)=0 and p′(0)≠0. Restricted the equal-norm hypothesis to nonzero roots and updated both docstrings and the module summary. The other two declarations are unchanged. The required compilation succeeded with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.

/-!
# Mean value problem

*Reference:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_value_problem)

  by *David Tischler*

namespace MeanValueProblem

/--
Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there is a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ |p'(z)|$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.degree) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ):
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
The following weaker version of the mean value problem has been proven.
Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ 4|p'(z)|$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_leq_4 (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.degree) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ):
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ 4 *‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
Tischler proved the following bound for a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d \ge 2$
with $p(0) = 0$, $p'(0) \ne 0$, and all roots real.
There is a critical point $c$ such that
$|p(c)|/|c| \le (d-1)/d \cdot |p'(0)|$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_of_real_roots (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.natDegree)
    (hp0 : p.eval 0 = 0) (hp0' : p.derivative.eval 0 ≠ 0)
    (h : ∀ x : ℂ, p.IsRoot x → x.im = 0) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval c‖ / ‖c‖ ≤ (p.natDegree - 1) / p.natDegree * ‖p.derivative.eval 0‖ := by
  sorry

/--
Tischler proved the following bound for a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d \ge 2$
with $p(0) = 0$, $p'(0) \ne 0$, and all nonzero roots having the same norm.
There is a critical point $c$ such that
$|p(c)|/|c| \le (d-1)/d \cdot |p'(0)|$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_of_roots_same_norm (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.natDegree)
    (hp0 : p.eval 0 = 0) (hp0' : p.derivative.eval 0 ≠ 0)
    (h : ∀ x y : ℂ, p.IsRoot x ∧ p.IsRoot y → x ≠ 0 → y ≠ 0 → ‖x‖ = ‖y‖) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval c‖ / ‖c‖ ≤ (p.natDegree - 1) / p.natDegree * ‖p.derivative.eval 0‖ := by
  sorry

end MeanValueProblem
